Accommodation & Hospitality Manager

Pink Roadhouse – Oodnadatta, South Australia

The Pink Roadhouse is seeking an experienced Accommodation & Hospitality Manager to oversee the day-to-day operation of our remote hospitality, accommodation and tourism business in Oodnadatta, South Australia.

This is a senior, hands-on management position involving responsibility across accommodation, café, licensed liquor, retail, tourism and a co-located Australia Post Licensed Post Office. It is not an entry-level management, shift-supervisor or general front-of-house position.

The successful applicant must relocate to and reside in Oodnadatta on an ongoing basis. This is not a fly-in fly-out or drive-in drive-out position.

Key responsibilities
Manage the daily operation of the roadhouse, café, licensed bar and accommodation facilities
Supervise, roster, recruit, train and performance-manage staff
Oversee liquor licensing, RSA, food-safety and WHS compliance
Act as a Responsible Person for the licensed premises once approved
Manage accommodation bookings, housekeeping standards and guest services
Manage stock control, purchasing, supplier relationships, margins and operating costs
Oversee cash handling, reconciliations, reporting and administrative processes
Oversee the co-located Australia Post Licensed Post Office, including customer transactions, mail and parcel services, reconciliations and compliance procedures
Resolve staffing, customer and operational issues independently
Develop and implement operational procedures
Support business planning and continuous operational improvement
Build respectful working relationships with local residents, Aboriginal community members, contractors and tourists
Essential skills and experience

Applicants must demonstrate:

At least two years’ experience in a comparable hospitality or accommodation management position
Management responsibilities extending beyond shift supervision or general hospitality duties
Experience managing a multi-faceted operation involving accommodation, food service and licensed hospitality
Proven responsibility for staff rostering, recruitment, training, supervision and performance management
Experience with stock control, purchasing, supplier management and cost control
Experience managing cash reconciliations, operational reporting and compliance procedures
The ability to make independent operational and staffing decisions without daily on-site direction
A demonstrated understanding of the practical requirements and limitations of living and working in a remote community
Willingness and ability to relocate to and reside in Oodnadatta on an ongoing basis
Availability to work weekends and public holidays as required by the management roster
Current Responsible Service of Alcohol certification, or the ability to obtain it before commencing
Eligibility and willingness to obtain and maintain South Australian Responsible Person approval
Ability and willingness to complete all required Australia Post training, accreditation and compliance requirements
Ability to obtain a satisfactory National Police Check and satisfy the probity requirements associated with Australia Post services and liquor-licensing responsibilities
Highly desirable experience
Previous experience living and working in a remote or very remote location
Experience working respectfully with Aboriginal communities, customers and community organisations
Experience managing both accommodation and licensed hospitality operations
Experience in an outback tourism, roadhouse or remote-area business
Experience operating or supervising an Australia Post Licensed Post Office, postal agency or comparable regulated service
Experience handling secure transactions, customer information and strict procedural compliance
Experience using point-of-sale, accommodation-booking, rostering and financial-reporting systems
Current South Australian Responsible Person approval
Current Australian driver’s licence
Current first-aid certification
Employment details
Full-time, ongoing position
Salary: $90,000 per annum plus superannuation
Accommodation may be available under a separate arrangement
Location: Oodnadatta, South Australia
Weekend and public-holiday work will form part of the management roster

Employment will be subject to a satisfactory National Police Check and completion of the required Australia Post and liquor-licensing approval processes.

Application requirements

Applicants must submit:

A current résumé
A cover letter addressing the essential criteria
Specific examples demonstrating their management responsibilities
Details of the size and type of hospitality or accommodation operations they have managed
Details of their staff-management, financial and compliance responsibilities
Details of any remote-area, Australia Post or comparable regulated-service experience
Confirmation that they understand the location and are willing to relocate to and reside in Oodnadatta

Applications that do not include a cover letter addressing the essential criteria may not progress to the next stage.

## ICT Support Technician
## Position Overview
We are looking for a motivated and technically proficient ICT Support Technician to join our team and provide reliable support across our computer infrastructure, software systems, and web technologies. In this role, you will be responsible for diagnosing and resolving technical issues, maintaining hardware and software environments, and ensuring end users receive timely and effective assistance. The ideal candidate is a proactive problem-solver with strong communication skills and a genuine passion for technology. This position suits someone who thrives in a fast-paced environment and is committed to delivering high-quality technical support.
## Key Responsibilities
- Assess software and hardware requirements to identify appropriate technical solutions and resolve user-reported problems effectively.
- Respond promptly to enquiries from staff regarding software and hardware issues, providing clear guidance and practical resolutions in a professional manner.
- Install, configure, and maintain approved software applications, ensuring systems remain up to date, secure, and aligned with organisational standards.
- Adapt and modify existing programs and system configurations to better meet the evolving needs of end users and business operations.
- Implement, configure, and monitor computer networks, supporting both wired and wireless infrastructure to maintain consistent connectivity across the organisation.
- Design, update, and maintain organisational websites, ensuring content accuracy, functionality, and a positive user experience.
- Repair and replace peripheral equipment such as printers, terminals, monitors, and modems, maintaining accurate records of assets and service activity.
- Provide first- and second-level technical support to end users, either in person, remotely, or via a helpdesk or call centre environment, logging all incidents and resolutions through the appropriate ticketing system.
- Promote the efficient and effective use of applications and equipment across teams, offering training and guidance where required.
- Collaborate with internal stakeholders and external vendors to escalate and resolve complex technical issues in a timely manner.
- Conduct routine system checks, preventative maintenance, and performance monitoring to minimise downtime and ensure infrastructure reliability.
- Maintain thorough technical documentation, including user guides, network diagrams, and records of system configurations and changes.
## Required Qualifications & Skills
- Certificate III or IV in Information Technology, or a relevant tertiary qualification in ICT, Computer Science, or a related discipline.
- Demonstrated experience in a technical support, helpdesk, or IT operations role.
- Solid understanding of computer hardware components, operating systems (Windows, macOS, Linux), and common business software applications.
- Experience installing, configuring, and troubleshooting software and peripheral devices.
- Working knowledge of networking fundamentals, including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, and LAN/WAN connectivity.
- Familiarity with web technologies and basic website maintenance, including content management systems.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to diagnose technical issues efficiently and accurately.
- Excellent verbal and written communication skills, with the ability to explain technical concepts clearly to non-technical users.
- Ability to manage competing priorities, work independently, and maintain composure under pressure.
- A customer-focused approach with a professional and courteous manner in all interactions.
## Preferred Qualifications
- CompTIA A+, Network+, or equivalent industry certification.
- ITIL Foundation certification or familiarity with ITIL service management principles.
- Experience working in a managed service provider (MSP) or enterprise IT environment.
- Exposure to cloud platforms such as Microsoft 365, Azure, or Google Workspace.
- Experience with remote desktop tools and helpdesk ticketing systems such as ServiceNow, Freshdesk, or Jira Service Management.
- Knowledge of cybersecurity best practices and endpoint protection solutions.
## Why Join Us?
- Be part of a collaborative and supportive team culture that values continuous learning and professional growth.
- Access ongoing training, certification support, and clear pathways for career advancement within the ICT field.
- Enjoy a stable, full-time permanent role with a competitive salary and superannuation package.
- Benefit from flexible working arrangements and a healthy work-life balance in a forward-thinking organisation.
- Work with modern technology and contribute to meaningful projects that directly support business operations and user experience.
## Job Details
- Job Type: Full-time, Permanent
- Work Schedule: 8-hour shift
- Salary: $70,000 – $120,000 per year + Super

Full-time Position

JOB TASKS AND RESPONSIBILITIES
•	Examining vehicle surfaces to determine the extent of paint damage and the preparation required prior to refinishing.

•	Blending newly applied paint with existing finishes to achieve an accurate colour match and seamless appearance.
•	Baking, curing, polishing and buffing painted surfaces to produce a high-quality finish.
•	Inspecting completed paintwork to ensure compliance with manufacturer specifications, company quality standards and customer expectations.

•	Maintaining spray booths, spray guns, compressors and painting equipment to ensure safe and efficient operation.
•	Ordering, handling and storing paints, thinners and other hazardous materials in accordance with workplace health and safety and environmental requirements.
•	Liaising with panel beaters and workshop staff to coordinate vehicle preparation and painting schedules.
•	Providing customers with updates on the progress of painting and refinishing work when required.
•	Travelling to various workshop locations throughout Australia to undertake vehicle painting and refinishing work as required.

EXPERIENCE
•	Minimum of 5 years of proven experience as a Vehicle Painter.
•	Demonstrated experience in automotive spray painting, colour matching and vehicle refinishing.
•	Experience repairing and refinishing vehicles affected by hail damage, collision damage and restoration projects.
•	Sound knowledge of automotive paint systems, surface preparation techniques and spray-painting equipment.
•	Ability to consistently produce high-quality finishes in accordance with manufacturer and industry standards.
•	Current and valid driver's licence with the ability to travel for vehicle collections and workshop requirements when necessary.
•	This role requires working at various workshop locations throughout Australia for periods of approximately 4–6 months. The successful candidate must therefore be available to travel and work interstate for extended periods.

Employment Basis: Full-Time

Specific Task
•	Operate specialize Kotzur bulk grain handling circuit to use for the receival, storage, transfer, packing, and dispatch of grain products.
•	Conduct detailed inspection of equipment, check and record any faults and rectified before operation (refer to maintenance schedule procedure).
•	Reference should be given to risk assessment of bucket elevator operation. Paying particular attention to that all safety guards and equipment are installed (refer to risk assessment).
•	Before putting drag conveyor into operation, ensure foreign material is removed from drag conveyor.
•	Ensure close all boots and inspection panels and ensure drive guards are in place.
•	Start conveyor motor and listen carefully if any abnormal noises before operation.
•	Conveyors should not be operated unless they are completely enclosed, and power transmission guards are in place.

•	Inspect chain, paddles, transmission v-belts.
•	Check chain tension, gearbox, bearing, all sheave drive and attaching parts, check all hardware, and check chain carrier tracks.
•	As per WHS requirements tests E-stops, control panels (refer to risk assessment operation).
•	Once bulk grain handling circuit is safe to operate, proceed to the test running the circuit with no grain.
•	Proceed to control room and test container inverter weight scales are reading correctly.
•	Carry out visual inspection of individual weight scales, frames, wiring are safe to operate.
•	Ensure twist locks on both inverter 1 and 2 are operating correctly.
•	Inspect and grease cylinders, pivot points and check safety guards are operating correctly.
•	Ensure area is clear of any obstacles (shovels, brooms, grains, water, etc) to move any trip hazard while loading.
•	Check fumigation clearance has been approved, and the area is safe.
•	Coordinate with export team members to ensure packing can commence.

General Task
•	Clean, repair as required and inspect containers to meet the standards of food quality of Department of Agriculture, Fisheries, and Forestry.
•	Report of any major faults of containers to site manager, so replace container can be organised.
•	Record individually containers specifications when received.
•	Follow site safety procedures and permit system.

Due to the recent and upcoming further expansion of our business operations, CH on Peel Pty Ltd (trading as Central Hospitality Group) requires additional full time Food and Beverage Attendants.

Our operations are situated at Tamworth, in North West NSW, and include:

* CH Boutique Hotel (62 rooms);
* Heritage listed DECO Wine Bar & Restaurant;
* Hopscotch Restaurant;
* The Pig & Tinderbox;
* The Pavilion Function and Conference Centre;
* The Bureau by Red Ribbon; and
* Dungowan Brewery

The Position

You will have an opportunity to further develop your hospitality skills and experience work in a variety of areas across our food service sites. The position includes attending to food and beverage duties and bar work. This position is suited for candidates that like to work in a fast-paced supportive team environment, with high quality table service experience preferred. The successful applicant must be available across a 7 day roster including nights and weekends.

As a member of our team, you will be responsible for the overall running of your designated sections of the venue, leading by example and maintaining high standards. You must be highly motivated and able to manage operational elements of the business from front to back of house. You will be passionate about your job, have a superior knowledge of food and beverage, understand the order of service, and ensure our clients leave having had an all-round unforgettable dining experience.

Key duties of this role include, but are not limited to the following:

* Explain the menu to guests, assisting those with special dietary needs or preferences as well as provide suitable assistance when recommending beverages
* Maximize sales opportunities by upselling items
* Ensure accuracy whilst ordering and delivering food and beverage orders
* Liaise with the Kitchen on special requests or delayed meals
* Clear and reset tables as well as ensuring service areas are clean and tidy
* Maintain standards of hygiene for food handling and presentation
* Promote a safe workplace by recognizing hazards and promoting general OHS practices

The Person

* RSA Certificate Essential
* Diploma is hospitality operations or similar is desirable but not required
* Previous Bar experience
* Experience in a fast-paced hospitality environment
* Great presentation and customer service skills
* Willingness to be part of an enthusiastic and motivated team
* Willingness to jump into any task required, cleaning, food preparation and customer service
* Strong awareness of Hygiene & Food Safety Standards
* Must always be well presented, have a great work ethic and the ability to perform well under pressure
* A Positive can-do attitude and the ability to work early mornings, late evenings, weekends and public holidays
* So, if you are a 'can-do' person, who thrives on new challenges; likes working in a team environment; and consistently delivers to the highest quality, then you'll fit right in and we'd like to have you on our team.

Salary range: $63,000 - $70,000 per year

  An exceptional opportunity is available to join a prestigious global organisation offering a flexible hybrid work model, excellent benefits, and a collaborative work environment.     
  In this role, you will research, translate, analyse, and summarise Australian news and current affairs content in Japanese for reporting to Head Office. Coverage areas include Australia-Japan relations, politics, economics, public policy, and geopolitical developments across Australia, New Zealand, and the Pacific Islands.     
  If you have experience in research, media monitoring, policy analysis, journalism, or related fields, we would love to hear from you.     
   Key Responsibilities      
 
  Conduct research and prepare concise reports, summaries, presentations, and briefings (Word, PowerPoint, etc.) for Head Office.     
  Monitor and analyse political, economic, and geopolitical developments across Australia, New Zealand, and the Pacific region.     
  Research industry developments in:      
  Critical minerals and mining     
  Energy (natural gas, coal, CCS)     
  Infrastructure (power, utilities, data centres, social infrastructure)

  Australia's engagement with the Pacific and ASEAN

  Travel within Australia, Pacific Island countries, and Japan as required, and prepare reports on findings and activities.

  Native-level or business-fluent Japanese with excellent Japanese writing and reporting skills.

  Background in journalism, media, research, government, consulting, public policy, international relations, economics, or a related field will be highly regarded.     
  Strong analytical, communication, and stakeholder management skills.     
  Ability to work independently and manage multiple priorities.     
  Unlimited Australian work rights (Australian Citizen, Permanent Resident, or Partner Visa holder).

  Competitive salary package.     
  Hybrid work arrangement (office and work-from-home flexibility).     
  Opportunity to work with a respected global organisation.     
  Exposure to international policy, business, and geopolitical issues.     
  Supportive, friendly, and collaborative working environment.     
  Domestic and international travel opportunities.

Job Advertisement


Chef – Full Time
Business: Nepalaya Hospitality Group Pty Ltd (ABN 29 639 400 963) trading as Namaste Sydney
Location: 307 Pitt Street, Sydney NSW 2000, Australia
Website: https://namasterestro.com.au/
Occupation: Chef (ANZSCO 351311)
Salary Range: AUD $75,000 – $85,000 per annum plus superannuation
Employment Type: Full-time (minimum 38 hours per week)

Job Published: 27 July 2026
Applications Close: 28 August 2026

ABOUT THE BUSINESS
Nepalaya Hospitality Group Pty Ltd, trading as Namaste Sydney, operates a well-established full-service restaurant in the heart of Sydney CBD and forms part of a growing hospitality group with multiple hospitality venues. The restaurant has established a strong reputation for delivering quality à la carte dining, exceptional customer service, and a consistently high standard of hospitality.
Operating within a modern commercial kitchen, Namaste Sydney offers a diverse à la carte menu prepared using quality ingredients and established culinary techniques. The restaurant caters to a broad customer base in a fast-paced dining environment and is committed to maintaining excellence in food quality, presentation, operational efficiency, and compliance with Australian food safety standards.
Due to continued business growth and increasing customer demand, Nepalaya Hospitality Group Pty Ltd is seeking an experienced Chef to support kitchen operations, contribute to menu development, maintain consistent food quality, and assist in delivering an exceptional dining experience.

ABOUT THE ROLE
The Chef will be responsible for planning, organising, and supervising food preparation and cooking activities within a busy commercial kitchen. Working collaboratively with management and kitchen staff, the successful candidate will ensure the consistent preparation and presentation of high-quality à la carte meals while maintaining operational efficiency, food safety compliance, and exceptional customer satisfaction.
The role requires a motivated hospitality professional with strong technical cooking skills, sound organisational capability, and the ability to coordinate kitchen activities during high-volume service periods. The successful candidate will also contribute to menu planning, food costing, stock management, quality assurance, and continuous improvement initiatives to support the efficient operation of the kitchen.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES
Core Culinary Operations
1.	Plan, organise and coordinate daily food preparation and cooking activities in accordance with operational requirements and anticipated service demands, ensuring kitchen readiness before each service period.
2.	Prepare, cook and present high-quality à la carte meals using a range of commercial cooking techniques while maintaining consistency in flavour, quality, presentation and portion control.
3.	Coordinate kitchen workflow during busy lunch and dinner services to ensure efficient meal production, timely service delivery, and effective communication between kitchen and front-of-house staff.
4.	Monitor food quality throughout all stages of preparation and service, ensuring ingredients are fresh and finished dishes consistently meet established quality standards.
5.	Maintain consistency in recipe execution, presentation standards and quality assurance across all menu offerings while ensuring customer expectations are consistently achieved.

Menu Planning and Development
1.	Assist in planning, reviewing and refining menus to maintain product quality, seasonal relevance and commercial competitiveness.
2.	Develop and recommend seasonal specials and new menu items based on customer preferences, market trends and ingredient availability.
3.	Support recipe standardisation, food costing and portion control to maximise operational efficiency while maintaining profitability.
4.	Evaluate customer feedback and menu performance to identify opportunities for continuous menu improvement and innovation.
5.	Participate in menu trials and product development initiatives to enhance the restaurant's culinary offerings.

Kitchen Operations and Inventory Management
1.	Manage inventory through effective ordering, receiving, storage and stock rotation procedures to maintain appropriate stock levels.
2.	Apply FIFO inventory management principles and monitor ingredient usage to minimise food wastage and maximise product quality.
3.	Conduct regular stocktakes and assist in monitoring food costs through effective inventory management practices.
4.	Liaise with suppliers regarding product quality, deliveries and stock availability to ensure uninterrupted kitchen operations.
5.	Maintain accurate purchasing, inventory and stock control records in accordance with business procedures.

Team Leadership and Kitchen Coordination
1.	Work collaboratively with kitchen and front-of-house teams to ensure efficient communication and coordinated service delivery.
2.	Support, mentor and provide day-to-day guidance to junior kitchen staff to maintain productivity, consistency and professional kitchen standards.
3.	Assist in allocating daily kitchen duties and coordinating workflow to maximise operational efficiency during service periods.
4.	Promote a positive, organised and team-oriented kitchen environment focused on quality, accountability and continuous improvement.
5.	Contribute to staff training by reinforcing food preparation techniques, food safety practices and operational procedures.

Food Safety, Hygiene and Compliance
1.	Maintain compliance with HACCP principles, NSW Food Authority requirements and all relevant food safety legislation.
2.	Ensure kitchen equipment, food preparation areas and storage facilities are maintained in a clean, organised and hygienic condition at all times.
3.	Monitor food storage temperatures, sanitation procedures and food handling practices to ensure ongoing compliance with regulatory requirements.
4.	Ensure compliance with Workplace Health and Safety obligations and the safe operation of commercial kitchen equipment.
5.	Maintain accurate food safety documentation, cleaning schedules and operational records to support regulatory compliance.


Operational Administration
1.	Complete kitchen records relating to stock usage, food safety, cleaning schedules and wastage reporting accurately and on time.
2.	Assist management in identifying opportunities to improve kitchen efficiency, food quality, operational productivity and customer satisfaction.
3.	Support continuous improvement initiatives designed to enhance restaurant operations, service standards and overall business performance.

MANDATORY REQUIREMENTS
1.	AQF Advanced Diploma or Diploma in Hospitality, Commercial Cookery or a closely related discipline.
2.	Minimum 2 years' full-time relevant experience as a Chef within a commercial restaurant environment.
3.	Demonstrated experience preparing and delivering high-quality à la carte cuisine within a busy commercial kitchen.
4.	Strong knowledge of HACCP principles, NSW Food Safety Standards and food handling legislation.
5.	Sound understanding of Workplace Health and Safety obligations within hospitality environments.
6.	Experience in menu planning, stock control, purchasing procedures and kitchen coordination.

KEY COMPETENCIES
1.	Strong culinary expertise across a broad range of commercial cooking techniques and food preparation methods.
2.	Demonstrated ability to coordinate kitchen operations during high-volume service periods while maintaining quality, consistency and efficiency.
3.	Sound understanding of menu development, food costing, recipe standardisation and portion control principles.
4.	Excellent organisational and time management skills with the ability to manage multiple competing priorities in a fast-paced environment.
5.	Leadership capability to supervise, mentor and support kitchen staff within a collaborative team environment.
6.	Strong communication and interpersonal skills when working with management, kitchen staff and front-of-house pers

Position: Marketing Specialist
Position Type: Full Time

Employer Name: PRASAD, SAJO - T/A Wings of Support
A.B.N: 19 738 723 048

Summary
Our client Wings of Support is seeking to add a Marketing Specialist to their dedicated team in Kununurra. Since launching in 2023, Wings of Support has been committed to empowering NDIS participants in the East Kimberley region. With a strong client-centred approach and a focus on culturally responsive care, the organisation is expanding its outreach and visibility through strategic marketing efforts tailored to remote and regional communities.

The typical job responsibilities will include, but are not limited to the following:
•	Plan and execute marketing campaigns to promote support services and outreach initiatives.
•	Develop culturally appropriate content for print, digital, and multimedia platforms.
•	Manage website updates, email campaigns, and social media accounts regularly.
•	Design and produce flyers, brochures, and community-specific promotional materials.
•	Collaborate with community stakeholders to coordinate local engagement events.
•	Use NDIA and DHAC dashboards to analyse market trends and identify service gaps.
•	Monitor campaign performance using Google Analytics and Meta Ads Manager.
•	Create participant-focused stories and content aligned with NDIS and aged care reforms.
•	Support grant applications with case studies and marketing data insights.
•	Build relationships with ACCHOs, Elders, and local councils across the Kimberley.
•	Represent the organisation at community expos and local awareness events.
•	Track referral numbers, participant enquiries, and enrolment data as part of reporting.
•	Ensure marketing materials are accessible, easy to read, and culturally safe.
•	Use tools like Canva or Adobe Suite for graphic design and brand consistency.
•	Stay informed on aged care reforms and NDIS policy changes affecting outreach.

Applicants must meet the following minimum requirements to be considered for the role:
•	Bachelor’s degree or equivalent experience in marketing, communications or community engagement.
•	Experience designing culturally appropriate materials for Aboriginal and remote communities.
•	Demonstrated ability to manage integrated digital and print campaigns from concept to execution.
•	Proficiency in using Google Analytics, Meta Ads Manager, and Mailchimp for performance tracking.
•	Familiarity with NDIS or aged care systems and current reforms relevant to participant engagement.
•	Strong writing skills with an ability to tailor content for diverse audiences and formats.
•	Capacity to work independently in fast-paced environments with multiple projects and deadlines.
•	Willingness to travel across the Kimberley region for outreach and community-based events.

Due to the volume of applicants, only those meeting the minimum standards will be considered and only successful candidates will be contacted.  Thank you for your interest in the role.
